_comment: Per-clip ingest config for the precompute pipeline (api/scripts/precompute.py). Carries the HUMAN knowledge the cache needs but Azure cannot produce: which .mov to read, the sampling window/fps the hero program replays over (must match hero_program.json's sample_frames so detect keys align), the known goal event, the jersey pins (hand-verified #10 -> p_messi), and which evidence frames become committed stills. The pipeline runs Azure detect over the sampled frames, mints det_ids, resolves pins to the nearest detection box (renaming that det to the pin's det_id), writes read_text under the renamed id, derives events[].scorer_det from the SAME pin resolution, and emits the cache in api/interpreter/cache.py's exact shape. See docs/cache-schema.md.

pins._comment: Hand-verified hero #10 (Messi). Matched AFTER detect to the nearest person box at frame 4625 (the conf-0.75 left box in the committed hero cache). The matched det is RENAMED to det_id 'p_messi'; read_text is written under that same id. Azure Read misreads the stylized WC numeral (22 -> 77) and gpt-4o vision is TPM-gated, so this stays pinned.
pins.note: Hand-verified. Azure Read misreads the stylized WC numeral (22 -> 77); gpt-4o vision pending TPM quota. The 10 is human-legible and pinned for the hero query (disclosed in the demo).

events._comment: Known goal moment. scorer_det references the pin det_id above; the pipeline derives the actual scorer_det from the resolved pin (NOT this literal) so it is byte-identical to a minted det_id that carries the #10 read_text. ts_ms 4000 is on the 8fps sampling stride (3500 + 4*125).

stills._comment: Evidence frames the unchanged web EvidencePanel.frameSrc() expects: ts<=4200 -> goal-4000.jpg, else scorer-4625.jpg. Each declares its output filename so the pipeline reproduces exactly those two files in web/public/frames/.
